checks.message: Verify the backup plan includes cross-region or cross-account copies for DR
checks.context: A backup in the same region as the source doesn't protect against regional failures or ransomware that has access to your account. Add a copy rule to a separate region or account.

checks.message: Backup vault not encrypted with a customer managed KMS key
checks.context: Backup vaults use an AWS-managed key by default. A CMK lets you control who can decrypt backups independently of who has access to the vault, and gives you a CloudTrail audit trail of every restore.

checks.message: Configure a vault lock policy to prevent backup deletion
checks.context: Without vault lock, anyone with backup:DeleteRecoveryPoint can delete your backups — including ransomware or a compromised admin account. Vault lock (WORM) makes backups immutable for a defined period.

checks.message: Vault deletion destroys all recovery points in it
checks.context: All backups stored in this vault are permanently deleted. You cannot delete a vault that contains recovery points — you must delete each recovery point first, which is itself a destructive operation.

checks.message: Recovery point deletion is permanent — verify this is not your only backup
checks.context: Deleting a recovery point removes that backup permanently. If this is the only backup of a resource and the resource is later corrupted or deleted, there is no recovery path.

checks.message: Verify the restore target is isolated from production until validation is complete
checks.context: Restoring directly into a production environment can overwrite live data or cause conflicts. Restore to a separate account or VPC, validate the data, then cut over.
